candidates.why_relevant: Halkbank AD Skopje's Turkish parent. Group-level announcements (technology programmes, subsidiary investments) are published here in Turkish before any MK-side visibility. candidates.why_relevant: Halkbank T.A.Ş. is Turkish state-controlled; procurement by Turkish public-sector entities is published on EKAP/ihale.gov.tr. A group-level IT or payments award to a Turkish contracting entity is the leading indicator of what later appears in the Skopje subsidiary. candidates.why_relevant: A cross-border, standing ARCHIVE of national procurement data for 35 jurisdictions including North Macedonia, harvested from national portals and TED. This is the single strongest answer to the 'notices removed from the MK portal after expiry' problem — historical MK notices and awards persist here in structured form.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Bulk download the MK dataset (JSON/CSV) and filter buyers/suppliers on banking and payments terms. NOTE: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 — non-commercial only; check licence fit before any commercial deliverable.

candidates.why_relevant: Registry entry documenting the MK OCDS dataset — download links (JSON/Excel/CSV), per-year and all-time coverage, publisher, licence and quality notes. The correct entry point for a reproducible bulk pull of historical MK procurement, including expired notices.

candidates.source_name: Internet Archive Wayback CDX Server API — e-nabavki.gov.mk capture index
candidates.why_relevant: Directly addresses the cell's archived/expired-notice angle: a CDX query against the MK e-procurement domain returns a capture index stretching back to 2007, letting expired or removed notice pages be recovered by timestamp. Confirmed to return data for this domain during scouting (liveness to be re-verified by the deterministic pass).
candidates.suggested_collection_method: CDX query with matchType=domain + filter=statuscode:200, collapse=digest; then fetch /web/<timestamp>/<url> for changed captures. Rate-limit politely. Repeat for arhiva.finance.gov.mk and the MK bank domains.

candidates.why_relevant: An officially maintained MK-side ARCHIVE domain preserving procurement notices and contracts that have been removed from the current finance.gov.mk estate. Exactly the class of retained-but-delisted material this cell is chartered to find.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Full crawl of the огласи-и-договори path (Cyrillic percent-encoded URLs); store PDFs; then diff against live e-nabavki records to find delisted items.

candidates.why_relevant: The ESJN 'realised contracts' functionality retains contract-execution records after the notice itself expires, and the institution grid enumerates contracting authorities. This is the MK-side counterpart to the archive angle and the baseline any cross-border/archive comparison must diff against.

negative_findings.description: Searched in Macedonian for tender/procurement pages on the MK subsidiary domains of the foreign parents in scope (nlb.mk, halkbank.mk, sparkasse.mk) using Cyrillic procurement vocabulary.
negative_findings.result_summary: No procurement, tender or supplier-notice section surfaced for any of the three MK bank sites. Results were dominated by recruitment notices ('оглас за вработување') and retail product pages — a strong reminder that in MK 'оглас' is a heavily polluted term meaning both tender notice and job advert.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: MK commercial-bank procurement appears to be largely invisible on the banks' own MK web estate, which pushes the whole cell's weight onto parent-side publication, regional aggregators and archives. It also means 'оглас' must always be paired with 'набавка'/'тендер' to be usable as a query term.

negative_findings.description: The cell brief names Şekerbank as a parent group. Attempted to confirm a Şekerbank (TR) ownership link to TTK Banka AD Skopje.
negative_findings.result_summary: No evidence of a Şekerbank–TTK Banka ownership relationship was found. Available profiles instead describe TTK Banka as formed in 2006 from the merger of Teteks Kreditna Banka and Tetovska Banka, with Teteks Group (~44%) and EBRD (25%, acquired October 2006) as major shareholders. This may be stale data and does not disprove a later transaction.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: If the Şekerbank link is wrong or historical, tracking Turkish parent-side procurement for TTK would waste collection budget; conversely, an unrecorded EBRD stake makes ECEPP a more important channel than assumed. The ownership chain must be pinned from MSE/NBRM filings before the parent-side watchlist is finalised.

negative_findings.description: Fetched the Erste Group Procurement page to locate a published tender or RFP feed for group suppliers.
negative_findings.result_summary: The page exposes supplier documents (NDA, audit questionnaire, scorecards, Supplier Code of Conduct) and describes centralised supply management, but publishes no tender notices and does not enumerate which subsidiaries or countries it serves.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Confirms that group-level buying at the Sparkasse/Erste side is a closed, invitation-based process. No notice-scraping strategy will work there; intelligence must come from supplier-side disclosures, code-of-conduct localisations, and vendor case studies instead.

negative_findings.description: Attempted to confirm nabavke.com's advertised Macedonian coverage and access model by direct fetch.
negative_findings.result_summary: The fetch returned only the page title; body content was not present in the server-rendered HTML, so country coverage, pricing and terms could not be established. Coverage claims (RS, ME, BA, MK, HR, SI) come from search-result snippets, not from the site itself.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Both leading regional aggregators are commercial and JS-heavy. Their real MK depth — and whether they retain expired notices, which is the whole point for this cell — is unknown and must be tested in a trial before any subscription spend.

negative_findings.description: Searched for evidence of a specific parent-group framework agreement (core banking, cards, payments) cascading to a North Macedonian subsidiary.
negative_findings.result_summary: No concrete framework-agreement document or award naming both a parent group and its MK subsidiary was located through open search in this pass.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The cell's core hypothesis — that group framework contracts are decided abroad and cascade to MK — remains a plausible but unevidenced structural assumption. It should be tested against NLB/Erste annual reports and vendor press releases rather than assumed in downstream analysis.

negative_findings.description: Query-term reliability assessment for Macedonian search.
negative_findings.result_summary: 'оглас' collides with job adverts; 'НЛБ'/'NLB' collides strongly with the UK Northern Lighthouse Board and Kenya's National Lottery Board in English search; 'Halkbank' collides with a Turkmen bank, a Serbian bank of the same name and a volleyball club; 'набавка' alone returns overwhelmingly public-sector (government) results rather than commercial-bank buying.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Any automated query fleet built for this cell needs disambiguating co-terms ('NLB Skupina', 'Халкбанк АД Скопје', 'јавна набавка' + 'банка') or it will drown in false positives.

coverage_gaps.description: No Albanian-language (sq) searching was performed, despite Albanian being an official language in North Macedonia and NLB and ProCredit both operating sibling banks in Kosovo where procurement material is published in Albanian.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add an Albanian query set ('tender', 'prokurim publik', 'njoftim kontrate', 'furnizues', 'bankë') covering NLB Banka Prishtina and ProCredit Bank Kosovo, plus Kosovo's e-procurement portal, as a sibling-market mirror of MK activity.

coverage_gaps.description: Parent-side procurement estates for several relevant MK bank owners were not examined: Stopanska Banka (NBG), Silk Road Bank / former Alpha Bank Skopje, Komercijalna banka (now NLB), and the Turkish Ziraat/Halk chain beyond the parent announcements page.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Extend the parent-group watchlist to all foreign-owned MK banks derived from the NBNM licensed-bank register, and check each parent's home-country procurement publication duty (esp. state-owned parents, which trigger national portal obligations).

coverage_gaps.description: Wayback CDX coverage was probed only for e-nabavki.gov.mk. No capture-index profiling was done for arhiva.finance.gov.mk, the MK bank domains, or the regional aggregators — nor was archive.today (which often captures JS-rendered pages the Wayback Machine misses) tested at all.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a systematic CDX profiling pass over the full MK domain watchlist, and add archive.today / Bing cache as complementary retrieval channels for JS-rendered notice pages.

coverage_gaps.description: Non-EBRD IFI channels were not covered: World Bank/IFC, EIB, KfW/DEG and EU IPA programmes all finance financial-sector and payments-infrastructure work in North Macedonia and each notifies procurement on its own portal, outside e-nabavki.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add IFC/World Bank procurement notices, EIB, KfW and the EU IPA/EU-funded-projects notice channels for North Macedonia to the source set.

coverage_gaps.description: The two most promising regional aggregators (nabavke.com, ekapija-tenderi.com) are subscription products whose MK depth, historical retention and terms of service were not established. Opentender.eu's data carries a CC BY-NC-SA non-commercial licence.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run trial evaluations of both aggregators against a known MK banking notice, and obtain a licensing determination on whether CC BY-NC-SA Opentender data can be used in a commercial market-intelligence deliverable before it is built into the pipeline.

coverage_gaps.description: Supplier-side evidence was not scouted at all — vendor press releases, case studies, reference lists and partner directories are often the only public trace of a closed group framework contract cascading into an MK subsidiary.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add a supplier-side sweep (core banking, card personalisation, ATM/POS, payment-switch vendors) for 'North Macedonia' / 'Skopje' references and group-wide rollout announcements.

brief: For this cell the usable intelligence sits almost entirely outside North Macedonia: MK subsidiary bank websites (nlb.mk, halkbank.mk, sparkasse.mk) publish no procurement notices at all, so the visible layer is parent-side (NLB d.d. javni razpisi in Slovenian; Erste Group Procurement in Vienna, which publishes supplier rules but no tenders; Halkbank T.A.Ş. Turkish announcements and potentially EKAP) plus IFI channels, above all EBRD's ECEPP, where MK-relevant contracts bypass the national portal entirely. The strongest archive answers are structural rather than ad hoc: Opentender.eu/DIGIWHIST holds a bulk OCDS dataset for North Macedonia (CC BY-NC-SA, non-commercial), TED's dataset explicitly extends to MK, the official arhiva.finance.gov.mk preserves delisted notices, and a Wayback CDX query on e-nabavki.gov.mk returns captures back to 2007. Commercial Balkan aggregators (nabavke.com, ekapija-tenderi.com) advertise Macedonian coverage and would give cross-border correlation of the same vendor appearing in several NLB or Sparkasse markets, but both are JS-rendered subscription products whose MK depth and retention are unverified. Two caveats should carry forward: the brief's Şekerbank–TTK ownership premise found no supporting evidence, and 'оглас' is badly polluted by job adverts, so MK query fleets must always pair it with 'набавка' or 'тендер'.
